top_choice_rationale: P001 (B010, Helpman and Melitz) is the only awarding proposal on the slate and rests on a distinct, mature and well-attributed discovery. Melitz (2003) moved trade analysis from industries to firms, generating selection into exporting, exporter premia, entry and exit, and within-industry reallocation that representative-firm trade theory does not produce. Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extends this to exporting versus foreign investment, so two names follow the intellectual structure. Firm-level data from many countries have tested these predictions for over twenty years. The costs are real: Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn are uncredited precursors or parallel contributors, and welfare magnitudes are sensitive to distributional assumptions. A narrow citation on mechanism and acknowledgement in the scientific background address these, so I judge the award clearly preferable to no award. I rely on my own recollection of the literature, not independent verification.
